method: LLM-based analysis of simulator implementation (examples/AFDX_V3/README.md) mapped against extracted rule categories. Categories are grouped into functional domains matching simulator components: Frame Structure, Switch, End System, Virtual Links, Redundancy, and Timing.

Frame Structure & Validation.description: Rules about Ethernet frame format, sizes, CRC/FCS, and frame-level validation. Directly tested by the Sending ES (58 tests) and Receiving ES (frame integrity suite, 10 tests).

Traffic Policing & Control.description: BAG enforcement, bandwidth allocation, traffic shaping. Tested by switch BAG policing (token bucket) and enhanced policing test suites (5+5 tests).

Switching.description: Switch forwarding, filtering, buffering, priority queuing, frame aging, operational modes. Core of the Switch test suite (46 tests covering validation, authorization, policing, forwarding, queuing, aging, buffer overflow, discard tracking).

Virtual Links.description: VL configuration parameters: VL ID, BAG values, Smin/Smax, priority, MAC addressing derived from VL ID. Fundamental to every simulation and test.

Redundancy.description: Dual-network architecture, accept-first policy, duplicate detection, sequence-based redundancy management. Tested by Redundancy Management suite (6 tests).

End System Behavior.description: End System transmission/reception rules, full-duplex requirement, performance metrics (latency, jitter bounds, processing rate). Tested across Sending ES and Receiving ES suites.

Timing & Performance.description: Latency bounds, jitter constraints, transmission timing. The simulator tracks per-VL latency and the fuzzer can introduce timing violations to test these bounds.

QoS & Sub-VL Queuing.description: Priority levels, quality of service, sub-VL scheduling and queue management. The switch implements 4 priority queues (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) and FIFO discipline.

AFDX Addressing.description: MAC addressing (AFDX multicast format 03:00:00:00:VL_HI:VL_LO), VL-based addressing, IP addressing format for AFDX (Class A private 10.0.0.0/8). Validated by the receiving ES.

Sequence Number & Integrity.description: Sequence number range (0-255), wraparound, gap detection, ordinal integrity within a VL. Tested by sequence handling suite (7 tests) and integrity checks.

Reception & Error Handling.description: Frame reception behavior, buffer overflow handling, error detection and reporting. The receiving ES generates structured error codes (100-800 range) for every validation failure.

IP/UDP Validation (in-frame).description: IP header validation (version, total length, TTL) and UDP header checks performed by the receiving ES as part of frame validation. The ES validates IP version=4, TTL=1 (AFDX default), and UDP port mapping.

TCP Transport Layer.reason: Simulator has no TCP stack. AFDX uses UDP for data transport.

ICMP Messages.reason: Simulator does not implement ICMP. No ICMP generation or processing.

Application-Level Ports & SAP.reason: Communication ports, SAP services, and port allocation are application-layer concepts above the AFDX network layer. The simulator operates at the frame/network level.

Data Encoding & Application Data.reason: Data alignment, encoding, and format rules apply to application payload content, not to network-level frame behavior.

IP Fragmentation & Reassembly.reason: AFDX prohibits IP fragmentation in normal operation. The simulator does not implement fragmentation/reassembly.

IP Routing & Options.reason: AFDX uses static VL-based forwarding, not IP routing. TTL management for routing and IP options are not applicable.

Configuration & Management Plane.reason: Network configuration management, SNMP monitoring, ARINC 615A are management-plane functions not exercised by frame-level fuzzing.

Physical Layer.reason: Physical port speed, auto-negotiation, and duplex settings cannot be tested by injecting frames into the simulator.

General / Architectural.reason: High-level architectural assertions (scalability, compliance, interoperability) are not directly testable constraints.

Application Services.reason: Sampling service, file transfer (TFTP), and similar application-level services are not part of the AFDX network simulation.

UDP/Broadcast (above frame level).reason: UDP socket behavior and IP broadcast address semantics are above the frame validation level implemented in the simulator.
